scenes.text: The world's first nuclear reactor was built in a squash court, under a football stadium, in the middle of Chicago.
It was called Chicago Pile One, under Stagg Field at the University of Chicago.
The team was led by physicist Enrico Fermi.
They stacked fifty-seven layers of graphite, almost four hundred tons, with uranium inside.
It had no radiation shield and no cooling system.
Instead, three young scientists stood on a platform with buckets of a cadmium solution, ready to flood it.
People called them the suicide squad.
On December second, nineteen forty-two, after a morning of tests, Fermi calmly called for lunch.
At three twenty-five that afternoon, the pile started the first human-made, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction.
It ran for twenty-eight minutes, at about half a watt.
That's far less than a single household light bulb.
To celebrate, they shared a bottle of Chianti, and signed its label.
Then physicist Arthur Compton phoned with a secret message: the Italian navigator has landed in the New World.
How were the natives, came the reply. Very friendly.
Would you have stood next to that pile? Tell me below.

title: The first nuclear reactor was built in a squash court ☢️
caption: On Dec 2, 1942, Enrico Fermi's team ran the first self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction in a squash court under a Chicago stadium. No shielding, no cooling, just a bucket squad.
